twoFactor.intro: With two-factor sign-in on, you'll be asked for a six-digit code from an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, etc.) in addition to your password. You'll also get eight single-use recovery codes for when you can't reach the app.
twoFactor.enabledIntro: Signing in to this account requires a code from your authenticator app in addition to your password.
twoFactor.noCodesLeft: All recovery codes have been used; if you lose access to the app, the account can only be recovered through support.
twoFactor.setupIntro: Enter this secret in your authenticator app or scan/add its URI, then enter the current six-digit code to confirm:
twoFactor.uriLabel: otpauth URI to add to your app
twoFactor.recoveryTitle: These codes are shown only this once
twoFactor.recoveryDesc: Each code works only once, and you can't view them again after closing this section. Store them somewhere safe — each one is accepted once at sign-in in place of an app code.
twoFactor.disableIntro: To turn it off, you need your current password and a valid code (from the app or a recovery code):

guarantee.title: What does this page guarantee?
guarantee.body: Signing out a device revokes its session on the server; even if that device's token was copied earlier, it's no longer accepted. Each device's "last activity" is recorded from that session's real traffic. If you don't recognize a device, sign it out and, for extra security, use "Forgot password" on the sign-in page to set a new password for your account.

mcp.title: AI clients (MCP)
mcp.intro: Connect Claude, ChatGPT or another MCP client to your WordPress sites. Site owners and admins can make changes. Sensitive requests appear in the site's Alerts for approval.
mcp.namePlaceholder: Name, e.g. Claude on my laptop
mcp.directEdit: Allow file edits without per-edit approval
mcp.directEditHint: This token connects only to the selected site and backs up existing files before editing. Choose specific paths or grant temporary access to all existing editable files. Creating a plugin requires separate approval. Requires DigiWP Ai Bridge 3.9.5 or later.
mcp.directPaths: Exact paths relative to wp-content, one file per line
mcp.noOwnedSites: There are no sites you own on this panel.
mcp.boundSiteUnavailable: The site assigned to this token is unavailable.
mcp.editWindowHint: Allow this token to edit existing files on the selected site for the duration you choose. Edits are logged and backed up. Creating a plugin, deleting files, and restoring files require separate approval. Requires DigiWP Ai Bridge 3.9.5 or later.
mcp.editWindowAllHint: This token can edit any existing file supported by DigiWP Ai Bridge in the site's plugins, themes, and must-use plugins during this window.
mcp.newTokenTitle: Copy it now — it is shown only once
mcp.urlWithTokenLabel: Address with the token inside (for clients that take only a URL)
mcp.urlWithTokenWarning: An address with the token inside works like a password: anyone who sees it can use it. Revoke it here if it leaks.
mcp.confirmRevoke: Revoke this token? Any AI client using it stops working immediately.

mcp.pageSubtitle: One address and a personal token for Claude, ChatGPT or any MCP client.

peer.title: Link with the other server
peer.intro: Have an account on the {server} panel too? Link the two accounts and one MCP token, here or there, reaches the sites of both.
peer.step1: Sign in on the {server} panel, open “AI clients (MCP)” and make a link code
peer.step2: Type that code here. It works once, for ten minutes.
peer.orMake: Or start here: make a code and type it on the {server} panel.
peer.linked: Linked with {email} on the {server} panel since {when}.
peer.linkedHint: Your MCP clients list that account's sites too (ids start with “peer:”). Each site still follows the rules of the server it lives on: sensitive actions wait for approval there.
peer.confirmUnlink: Unlink the two accounts? MCP clients stop seeing the other server's sites right away.
